seo.title: Wan 3 AI Video Generator: Text, Image and References
seo.description: Learn when to use Wan 3 for text-to-video, image animation or mixed reference direction, with current constraints, prompting guidance and canonical pricing.

overview: Wan 3 is the current standard route in the Wan family for teams that want one model across text, image and reference-led production. Alibaba/Tongyi owns the model; MaxVideoAI distributes these launch endpoints through Fal rather than claiming a direct Alibaba integration.

hero.title: Wan 3
hero.subtitle: Create from text, animate an opening image, or direct a clip with mixed references across 480p, 720p and 1080p outputs.
hero.paragraph: Choose Wan 3 when a project needs a flexible current Wan workflow without automatically moving to the Prime tier. It accepts prompts, opening and optional ending frames, and a reference collection that can contain images, clips, audio, a file, or a public web page under the mode rules. Alibaba/Tongyi is the model owner, while Fal distributes execution for this MaxVideoAI launch.

features.title: Text direction for planned scenes
features.body: Describe the subject, setting, main action, camera path and final beat in a clear order. Wan 3 can render between two and thirty seconds, so the prompt should match the chosen length instead of overloading a short clip.

features.title: Opening and ending frame control
features.body: Animate a start image and add an end image when the final composition matters. Keep the motion instruction focused on the transition between those two visual anchors.

features.title: Mixed reference workflow
features.body: Reference mode can combine supported images, videos and audio, or use one eligible file or public page when thinking is enabled. Keep every source purposeful and within the documented count and duration limits.

features.title: Resolution chosen per delivery
features.body: Use 480p for inexpensive exploration, 720p for review, or 1080p when the approved composition needs a higher-resolution output. The displayed quote updates from the same canonical pricing calculation used at generation.

decisionCards.title: Best fit: one flexible Wan route
decisionCards.body: Pick Wan 3 for storyboards, product motion and character scenes that may move between prompt-only, image-led and reference-led direction during iteration.

decisionCards.title: Not ideal: an automatic premium choice
decisionCards.body: Do not assume Prime is required for every brief. Compare the siblings when procurement, review standards or a premium production path justify a separate choice.

decisionCards.title: Plan references before prompting
decisionCards.body: Assign each source a role such as identity, motion, rhythm or context. A smaller, intentional set is easier to diagnose than unrelated media gathered without hierarchy.

referenceWorkflows.title: Text-to-video
referenceWorkflows.body: Build a readable scene around one subject, one primary action and one camera move, then state the closing beat.

referenceWorkflows.title: Image-to-video
referenceWorkflows.body: Protect the uploaded composition while describing only the movement, camera behavior and environmental response that should develop.

referenceWorkflows.title: Reference-to-video
referenceWorkflows.body: Use at least one valid reference and respect the separate limits for images, clips, audio, files and public pages.

referenceWorkflows.title: Safety and rights
referenceWorkflows.body: Use media you are allowed to process, avoid deceptive likeness use, and review every output for unintended text, identity drift or unsafe details.

tabs.label: Scene
tabs.title: Define a readable scene
tabs.description: Establish subject, place and visible change before adding camera language.
tabs.copy:
Subject and setting:
[Who or what is visible, where the scene takes place, and the defining details]

Primary action:
[One observable action with a clear cause and result]

Final beat:
[The composition or movement that closes the clip]

tabs.label: Camera
tabs.title: Direct motion and timing
tabs.description: Match camera complexity to the chosen duration.
tabs.copy:
Camera start:
[Framing, lens feel and starting position]

Camera path:
[One controlled pan, track, push or orbit]

Motion rhythm:
[Speed, pauses and environmental reaction]

Continuity:
[Identity, wardrobe, props, lighting and screen direction]

tabs.label: References
tabs.title: Assign each reference a role
tabs.description: Explain what the model should take from every source.
tabs.copy:
Identity source:
[Reference and exact trait to preserve]

Motion source:
[Reference and movement to borrow]

Audio or rhythm source:
[Reference and timing role]

Avoid:
[Conflicting identities, unsupported combinations, unwanted text and watermarks]

tabNotes.body: A short prompt with a visible change is easier to evaluate than a list of unrelated events.
Use one deliberate camera path for short clips and sequence additional beats only when duration allows.
Reference mode still needs a hierarchy: name the source that controls identity, motion or rhythm.

globalPrinciples: Describe observable actions instead of abstract mood alone.
Keep the subject count small when continuity matters.
State the final beat so motion settles rather than stopping abruptly.
Treat consent, likeness rights and source ownership as part of the production brief.
engineWhy: Wan 3 unifies prompt-only, frame-led and mixed-reference choices under one current family route.
Longer duration options make it possible to plan a simple progression instead of compressing every beat.
Separate reference categories let a team diagnose which source controls identity, motion or sound.

demo.title: Wan 3 controlled product story
demo.prompt: A ceramic desk lamp sits in a quiet design studio at dawn. A hand rotates its dimmer, warm light grows across the textured wall, and the camera makes one slow lateral track before settling on the illuminated shade. Preserve the lamp proportions, natural hand anatomy and soft blue morning ambience. No logo, caption or watermark.
notes: The action has one cause and a visible environmental response.
The closing composition gives the clip a stable final beat.

proofItems.title: Identity continuity
proofItems.body: Check whether the main subject remains recognizable through motion and camera change.

proofItems.title: Readable motion
proofItems.body: Review contact, weight, environmental response and the final settling beat.

proofItems.title: Reference fidelity
proofItems.body: Compare the output with the intended identity, movement and context sources.

proofItems.title: Delivery quality
proofItems.body: Inspect composition, texture and temporal stability at the selected resolution.

proofItems.title: Editorial review
proofItems.body: Reject unwanted text, watermarks, unsafe imagery or unapproved likeness use.
